newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares start firm, seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares start firm, seen recovering.

text.p: Greek shares opened firm after a strong show on Friday with talk of an upcoming tax on interest earned on state securities boosting the case for equities and brokers expecting a market recovery.
Construction and industrials led the advance on Friday with banks and small-caps also trading stronger.

"The upcoming taxation of T-bills and government bonds will have a significant implication on large bond portfolios as the new level of T-bill rates is used as a base rate for FRN renewals," said Telesis Securities in its weekly outlook.
"This may trigger speculation on bank stocks this week. If the 1997 budget is credible, good corporate performance will be backed by lquidity flows leading to a sustained recovery," it said.

Friday's upside reaction came amid expectations that the government is planning to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds as the market awaits the 1997 budget.
The finance ministry has cut 40 basis point off the marker 12-month T-bill, down to 12.30 percent. The issue came to market on Thursday and sold very well.
National Bank of Greece said on Friday it is trimming its savings deposit rate by 25 basis points down to 11.25 percent effective November 4.

"There is good news out there but the market was not reacting. A stable economic policy, a likely tax on interest income earned on state debt paper, I think we're bound to see a pent up reaction by the equities market soon," said another broker.
The Athens general share index was trading 0.51 percent, or 4.75 points higher at 943.77 from Friday's 938.21 close after opening at 938.77 points.
Banks were up 0.87 percent, industrials trading 0.17 percent firmer with construction rebounding 0.93 percent. Small-caps were also up 0.41 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 593-611. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 25 drachmas at 4,225.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $10.63-$11.63. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,231-4,498 drachmas in early trade.
